# Rules for each kind of content

Draft. Matteo is reviewing these in the tone check (see `decisions.md`). Until he answers, follow them as written.

All of them sit on top of `voice.md` and `compliance.md`.

## Slides and decks

- One message per slide, written as a full-sentence title.
- One big number at most per slide.
- A source line on every slide with data.
- Ink title slide, white content slides. Start from the deck template (`links.md`).

## Company posts on X and LinkedIn

- The point or the number first, then two or three short lines, then the view.
- No emoji or hashtags. The account says "we".
- App screenshots show their date and never a gain.

## Matteo's own posts

- His voice and "I". The same rules for numbers.
- Anything about Doefin markets follows `compliance.md` like any other public piece.

## Newsletter

- One email per difficulty adjustment.
- One number first, then three short items with their sources, then the disclaimer.
- The subject line carries the news.

## Glossary

- A plain, factual definition under 160 characters, with no product language.
- Then a longer explanation and one worked example.

## Research notes and articles

- The main number in the first third.
- Every figure with its source and date, marked Measured, Single source or Judgement.
- Our own misses published first.

## Help docs

- "You", short steps, one task per page.
- A warning comes before the step it affects.

## Tool text

- One line on what the tool does, who it is for and who it is not for.
- A hint under each input and a live sentence that reads the result.

## Emails to partners and investors

- The first line says why you are writing. Then the context, then one ask.
- Signed with a first name.

## Announcements

- What changed, for whom and from when.
- No "thrilled" and no "game-changing". A claim like "first" needs proof on file.

## App text

- Buttons start with a verb.
- Errors say what happened and what to do next.
- Confirmations repeat the button's words.
